# statement: # ---- 00-overview/01-system-model.md ----
The engine has six components: five form the pipeline and the sixth exists to make the pipeline acyclic.
L0 is stateful by definition and holds everything that survives a tick: realised peak, tariff qualification state, commitment ledger, V(SOC).
L1 Belief is a pure read over immutable data and is the single source of truth about the world as known at a point in time.
L2 Valuation is a pure function mapping beliefs to linearizable economic primitives.
L3 Planner is a pure function given a solver seed, mapping primitives and commitments to order intent.
L4 Execution is an external, pre-existing simulator that maps order intent to market outcomes.
L5 Settlement is a pure function mapping outcomes to ex-post truth, P&L attribution and error decomposition.
L1, L2, L3 and L5 being pure functions of their declared inputs is what makes every seam independently recordable, replayable and property-testable.
Any hidden state in L2 or L3 destroys the independent recordability, replayability and property-testability of every seam.
The one-directional flow L1 to L2 to L3 to L4 to L5, as drawn, is not acyclic.
λ_SOC is a dual variable of the Planner's own optimisation, so Valuation cannot compute it without solving the Planner's problem.
PeakView prices the marginal kW of grid peak, which requires the peak already realised in the current accounting period, and that is a Settlement output.
The §19(2) qualification state — accumulated full-load hours and HLZF exposure — is realised history.
λ_SOC and peak_to_go are both feedback edges from downstream components to upstream components.
All feedback is strictly forward within a tick and lagged across ticks, passing through L0.
Within a single tick every arrow in the component graph points right.
L0 is read at the top of the tick and written at the end of the tick.
No component reads a value written later in the same tick.
Acyclicity within a tick is machine-checkable by the T3 acyclicity audit.
L2 publishes the value function V(SOC) as a concave piecewise-linear curve and does not publish a scalar λ_SOC.
V(SOC) is produced by the slow loop and read from L0.
The Planner obtains λ_SOC endogenously as the subgradient of V at the optimal terminal SOC.
Publishing V(SOC) rather than a scalar λ_SOC removes the circularity between Valuation and Planner.
Publishing V(SOC) is strictly more accurate than marking a scalar, because it prices the whole SOC distribution rather than a linearisation around a guess.
The engine is driven by four distinct clocks, not one loop: C_accounting, C_slow, C_gate and C_tick.
Each of the four clocks has a different information set and a different irreversibility.
C_accounting runs on the month and year boundary and drives peak accounting reset and §19(2) qualification evaluation.
A qualification lost in an accounting period is lost for that period and cannot be recovered.
C_slow runs daily or on material state change, drives recomputation of V(SOC, peak_state, qualification_state) and recalibration of the fill and activation models, and is cheap to redo.
C_gate is market-defined, drives binding submissions, and a submission becomes a commitment binding at the gate.
C_tick is event-driven and sub-gate, drives continuous intraday re-optimisation and dispatch, and its decisions are reversible until the ID gate.
Gate times are configuration and never code, living in a MarketCalendar loaded from data, versioned, and replayed with the backtest.
Market rules change, so a market rule change must be a data change and not a code change.
Every solve is stamped with the clock that triggered it, and the clock stamp is part of the content hash of the resulting plan.
Two solves at the same wall time triggered by different clocks are different artefacts.
C_slow output is an input to the Planner and never a dependency, so the Planner never blocks on the slow loop.
If the slow loop has not run, the Planner uses the last valid V(SOC) with a staleness penalty.
Each seam exists because the two sides have different rates of change, different failure modes, or different testability.
Belief changes when data sources change and Valuation changes when economics change.
Crossing the C1 seam with raw arrays would let a data-source change silently alter a price.
The C1 contract carries values and quality metadata and never handles into Belief storage.
C2 is the seam that carries the most design load.
Valuation knows economics but not feasibility, and the Planner knows feasibility but must not re-derive economics.
C2 carries linearizable primitives so that Valuation can express non-linear economics without the Planner needing to know what a bid curve is.
L4 Execution is a pre-existing, strategy-independent simulator.
The Planner emits intent — what orders, at what price and volume, with what validity — and nothing about how they are routed.
Emitting intent keeps the Planner testable without a market and keeps the simulator replaceable by a real venue adapter.
Settlement can reconstruct ex-post truth from fills, activations and meter data alone, with no access to what the Planner intended.
Denying Settlement access to Planner intent is what prevents ex-post accounting being contaminated by ex-ante belief.
C5 Settlement to State is the only backwards edge in the system.
C5 carries realised peak, qualification progress, closed commitments and the error attribution that feeds the slow loop.
L4 exists and is fixed, and this specification treats it as an external system with a defined adapter.
Forecasts enter the engine through L1 as data with declared provenance and quality.
Model training is an offline concern and the engine consumes forecast artefacts rather than fitting them online.
v1 is a single site, single POI, single battery system.
Multi-asset operation is anticipated in the contracts by keying every quantity by AssetId and PoiId, but is not designed for.
Sub-second dispatch and aFRR activation response are a separate, simpler control layer downstream of the Planner's setpoints.
# ---- 00-overview/02-conventions.md ----
There are two distinct sign reference frames and they must never be conflated.
In the battery frame p_batt > 0 is discharge, the battery delivering energy, and p_batt < 0 is charge, the battery absorbing energy.
The battery sign convention aligns with the market convention that a positive traded quantity is a sale, so every market-facing quantity shares the sign of p_batt.
In the POI frame p_poi > 0 is import from the grid and p_poi < 0 is export to the grid.
The Leistungspreis, §19(2) StromNEV and all network charges are levied on import peak.
The quantity the tariff measures must have the sign that makes peak a maximum rather than a minimum.
The POI bridge is p_poi[t] = load[t] − Σ_k ( pv_avail[t,k] − q[t,k] ) − p_batt[t], in kW slot-average.
pv_avail is a belief about available generation and q ≥ 0 is curtailed generation, which is a decision.

Writing the POI bridge without q makes the generation allocation an equality over non-negative terms, which is infeasible whenever available PV exceeds load plus charge headroom plus the export limit.
The condition under which the q-free bridge is infeasible is an ordinary condition, not an edge case.
Losses are inside p_batt.
The sign frames are enforced as distinct C# value types BatteryPowerKw, PoiPowerKw, LoadKw and PvKw, which do not implicitly convert.
The POI bridge is the only sanctioned conversion between the two frames and lives in exactly one place.
Typed sign frames cost a little ceremony and eliminate an entire bug class.
Power is in kW with type *PowerKw; site scale is kW while aFRR is quoted in MW, converted at the market adapter only.
Energy is in kWh with type EnergyKwh.
Reserve capacity is in MW with type ReserveMw and is never mixed with kW types.
Energy price is in EUR/MWh with type EnergyPrice, by market convention, and not EUR/kWh.
Reserve capacity price is in EUR/MW/h with type CapacityPrice, per hour of the product block.
Network peak price is in EUR/kW/period with type PeakPrice, where the period is a year or a month depending on the regime.
Tariff components — levies, taxes and surcharges — are normalised to EUR/MWh with type EnergyPrice.
SOC is in kWh with type EnergyKwh, absolute and never percent internally.
SOC as a fraction 0..1 with type SocFraction is presentation only and never appears in the objective.
Efficiency is a one-way fraction 0..1 with type Efficiency, and round-trip efficiency is η_c · η_d.
Duration is a slot count integer with type SlotSpan and is never seconds in business logic.
The objective function is denominated in EUR and nothing else.
Every term converts to EUR at its own boundary, and a term that emits anything else is a contract violation.
kW to MW conversion happens only at market adapters, is a typed operation, and there is exactly one 1000.0 in the codebase per direction.
Losses are charged at the battery terminal, one-way, on each direction.
The SOC state equation is soc[t+1] = soc[t] + Δt · ( η_c · p_charge[t] − p_discharge[t] / η_d ).
Battery power decomposes as p_batt[t] = p_discharge[t] − p_charge[t] with p_charge[t] ≥ 0 and p_discharge[t] ≥ 0.
Charge and discharge must be separate non-negative variables whenever η < 1, because a single signed variable lets the optimiser round-trip for free through the loss term.
With η_c · η_d < 1 and non-negative energy prices, simultaneous charge and discharge is never optimal.
Because simultaneous charge and discharge is never optimal under those conditions, the complementarity constraint is usually redundant and can be omitted.
The complementarity constraint is not redundant when negative prices, an aFRR activation obligation, or a peak-driven incentive to import make burning energy profitable.

The simultaneity policy is to omit the binary by default, enable it under a configuration flag, and run an invariant monitor that alerts whenever a solution contains simultaneous charge and discharge above tolerance.
Omitting the simultaneity binary by default gives LP-speed in the common case and correctness detection in the rare one.
Auxiliary load — HVAC, BMS, standby — is modelled explicitly as a LoadKw component rather than folded into η, so it appears in the POI balance and therefore in the peak.
The canonical resolution is 15 minutes, the market time unit.
SlotId is an int64 count of quarter-hours since the Unix epoch in UTC, and is monotone, gap-free and DST-independent.
All internal timestamps are UTC and there are no local-time fields in any contract.
Tariff logic is not UTC: Hochlastzeitfenster, monthly and annual peak accounting, and §19(2) qualification are defined on the Europe/Berlin civil calendar.
A civil day has 92, 96, or 100 quarter-hour slots depending on DST transitions, so any code that assumes 96 is wrong twice a year.
The DST spring-forward day has a nonexistent local hour and the autumn transition has a repeated local hour, and repeated local times are distinguished only by UTC offset.
Month boundaries for peak accounting are local-midnight boundaries, which are not fixed UTC offsets across the year.
A CivilCalendar service is the only component permitted to map SlotId to local date, local time and tariff window.
The CivilCalendar is backed by a pinned IANA tzdata version recorded in the run manifest, because tzdata itself changes and a backtest must be reproducible.
Every calendar-dependent test includes both DST transition days as fixtures.
H_plan, the Planner's optimisation horizon, must span at least to the end of the current accounting period in value terms.
H_plan does not span to the end of the accounting period: it is truncated, and the truncation is priced by V(SOC) and by the peak state carried in L0.
The truncation of H_plan is why the value function is not optional.
H_hot, the Belief hot window, satisfies H_hot ≥ H_plan and bounds memory.
Every fact carries two times: valid_time, the slot the fact is about, and knowledge_time, when the engine learned it.
A read is always of the form Get(series, valid_time, as_of: knowledge_time).
There is no API that returns a fact with knowledge_time greater than as_of.
The bitemporal read discipline is structural rather than disciplinary, and it is what makes backtests trustworthy.
Contract DTOs are named as a <Seam><Payload> record.
Valuation views are named <Lever>View.
Emitted terms are named <Shape>Term.
Invariants are named INV-<layer>-<nn>.
Test levels are named T0 to T6.
Decisions are named ADR-nnn.
Contracts are named C0 to C5.
Degradation modes are named in UPPERCASE.
The invariant layer letters are D for Belief/data, V for Valuation, P for Planner, X for Execution boundary, S for Settlement, T for Time/calendar and G for Global.
Storage and transport use float32 for forecast ensembles and price series where the source precision does not justify more.
Storage and transport use float64 for money, SOC, and anything entering the objective.
NaN is never a valid value in a contract, and missing is expressed by an explicit quality or provenance field rather than by a sentinel.
Money comparisons use an absolute tolerance of 1e-6 EUR and power comparisons an absolute tolerance of 1e-6 kW.
The numeric comparison tolerances live in one constants file and are referenced, never re-typed.
Rounding to market tick sizes and lot sizes happens once, at the order intent boundary C3, and the rounded value is what Settlement reconciles against.
Rounding to tick and lot sizes earlier than C3 corrupts the optimality gap measurement.
# ---- 00-overview/03-mispel-reference.md ----
Basisfall A1 "Stromspeicher" is one Entnahme-/Einspeisestelle, one EE-Anlage, one Stromspeicher without Ladepunkt, plus sonstiger Verbrauch.
A1 is measured by two quarter-hour-accurate Zweirichtungszähler, Z1 at the grid point and Z2 at the storage.
Sonderfall A5 is A1 with several gleichartige EE-Anlagen behind one Einspeisestelle, settled over a joint measurement per § 24 Abs. 3 (i.V.m. § 19 Abs. 3 S. 2 Halbsatz 2) EEG.
Measurement in A5 is unchanged from A1: Z1 and Z2 suffice.
The sole addition in A5 is the leistungsgewichteter Zuordnungs-Faktor ZF, splitting the förderfähige Netzeinspeisung per plant so each is settled at its own AW.
In A5 the Saldierung, the Speicherverluste and the umlagebelasteter Netzbezug are determined as in A1.
The scope is the Abgrenzungsoption only, with no Pauschaloption and no Ausschließlichkeitsoption.
PV is in Direktvermarktung only, with no Volleinspeisung, no Indifferenzbereich, no Ladepunkt and no A2, A3, A4 or A6.
Energy carries two labels only: green and grey.
Z1NB¼ is the Netzbezug at the Entnahmestelle, in kWh per quarter-hour.
Z1NE¼ is the Netzeinspeisung at the Einspeisestelle, in kWh per quarter-hour.
Z2V¼ is the Verbrauch im Stromspeicher, in kWh per quarter-hour.
Z2E¼ is the Erzeugung im Stromspeicher, in kWh per quarter-hour.
AW¼ is the anzulegender Wert of the EE-Anlage, in EUR/MWh per quarter-hour.
Px_inst is the installierte Leistung of EE-Anlage x per § 24 Abs. 3 S. 2 Halbsatz 2 EEG, in kW, and is static.
For gleichartige Windenergieanlagen an Land, Referenzertrag or Standardertrag is used in place of installierte Leistung per § 24 Abs. 3 S. 2 Halbsatz 1 EEG.
ZF is the leistungsgewichteter share of the Netzeinspeisung assigned to one plant, a static fraction between 0 and 1.
∑M sums over the quarter-hours of a calendar month and ∑J sums over the months of a calendar year.
Monthly and yearly boundaries in the delineation machinery are Europe/Berlin civil-calendar boundaries.
Within the A1/A5 scope (14) is identical to (14)A1 and (19) is identical to (19)A1,A4, so (20) carries no case distinction.
Formula (1)¼ = MIN[ Z1NB¼ ; Z2V¼ ] is the zeitgleicher Netzstromverbrauch im Stromspeicher.
Formula (2)¼ = MIN[ Z1NE¼ ; Z2E¼ ] is the zeitgleiche Netzeinspeisung aus dem Stromspeicher.
Formula (23)¼ = Z1NE¼ − (2)¼ is the grundsätzlich förderfähige zeitgleiche Netzeinspeisung direct from the EE-Anlage, before the AW>0 condition is applied.
Formula (24)¼ = WENN[ AW¼ > 0 ; 1 ; 0 ] is the AW>0 indicator of the quarter-hour.
Formula (25)¼ = (24)¼ · (23)¼ is the förderfähige zeitgleiche Netzeinspeisung direct from the EE-Anlage in AW>0 hours.
Formula (27)¼ = (24)¼ · (2)¼ is the zeitgleiche Netzeinspeisung aus dem Stromspeicher in AW>0 hours.
Formula (3) = ∑M Z1NB¼ is the gesamter Netzbezug.
Formula (4) = ∑M Z1NE¼ is the gesamte Netzeinspeisung.
Formula (5) = ∑M Z2V¼ is the Verbrauch im Stromspeicher.
Formula (6) = ∑M Z2E¼ is the Erzeugung im Stromspeicher.
Formula (9) = ∑M (1)¼ is the zeitgleicher Netzstromverbrauch im Stromspeicher.
Formula (10) = (5) − (9) is the zeitgleicher Verbrauch von EE-Strom im Stromspeicher.
Formula (11) = ∑M (2)¼ is the Basiswert der zeitgleichen Netzeinspeisung aus dem Stromspeicher.
Formula (12) = MAX[ (6) − (5) ; 0 ] is the Fremdtankstrom.
Formula (13) = MAX[ (11) − (12) ; 0 ] is the berücksichtigungsfähige zeitgleiche Netzeinspeisung aus dem Stromspeicher.
Formula (14)A1 = (6) / (5) is the Wirkungsgrad der Stromspeicherung.
Formula (15) = (14) · (10) is the EE-Speichererzeugung.
Formula (16) = MAX[ (13) − (15) ; 0 ] is the saldierungsfähige Netzeinspeisung.
Formula (17)A1 = MAX[ (5) − (6) ; 0 ] is the Verluste im Stromspeicher.
Formula (18) = (16) / (6) is the share of the saldierungsfähige Netzeinspeisung in der Speichererzeugung.
Formula (19)A1 = (18) · (17) is the privilegierungsfähige Stromspeicherverluste per § 21 EnFG.
Formula (20) = MIN[ (16) + (19) ; (3) ] is the umlagereduzierende Strommenge.
Formula (21) = (3) − (20) is the umlagebelasteter Netzbezug.
Formula (26) = ∑M (25)¼ is the förderfähige Netzeinspeisung direct from the EE-Anlage in AW>0 hours.
Formula (28) = MIN[ (13) ; (15) ] is the grundsätzlich förderfähige Netzeinspeisung von EE-Speichererzeugung, before the AW>0 condition is applied.
Formula (29) = ∑M (27)¼ is the zeitgleiche Netzeinspeisung aus dem Stromspeicher in AW>0 hours.
Formula (30) = (29) / (11) is the AW>0-Anteil der zeitgleichen Netzeinspeisung aus dem Stromspeicher.
Formula (31) = (30) · (28) is the förderfähige Netzeinspeisung von EE-Speichererzeugung in AW>0 hours.
Formula (32) = (26) + (31) is the insgesamt förderfähige Netzeinspeisung.
Formula (22) = ∑J (21) is the umlagebelasteter Netzbezug im Kalenderjahr.
Formula (33) = ∑J (32) is the insgesamt förderfähige Netzeinspeisung im Kalenderjahr.
In A5 the formulas (2)¼, (11), (23)¼ and (28) are reused unchanged and refer to the sum of the jointly measured plants.
Formula (ZFx) = Px_inst / (Pa_inst + Pb_inst) is the Zuordnungs-Faktor of plant x.
Formula (23x)¼ A5 = (ZFx) · (23)¼ is the grundsätzlich förderfähige zeitgleiche Netzeinspeisung attributed to plant x.
Formula (24x)¼ = WENN[ AWx¼ > 0 ; 1 ; 0 ] is the AWx>0 indicator of plant x.
Formula (25x)¼ = (24x)¼ · (23x)¼ is the förderfähige zeitgleiche Netzeinspeisung of plant x in AWx>0 hours.
Formula (27x)¼ = (24x)¼ · (2)¼ is the zeitgleiche Netzeinspeisung aus dem Stromspeicher in AWx>0 hours.
Formula (26x) = ∑M (25x)¼ is the monthly förderfähige Netzeinspeisung direct from plant x.
Formula (28x)A5 = (ZFx) · (28) is the grundsätzlich förderfähige Netzeinspeisung von EE-Speichererzeugung attributed to plant x.
Formula (29x) = ∑M (27x)¼ is the monthly zeitgleiche Netzeinspeisung aus dem Stromspeicher in AWx>0 hours.
Formula (30x) = (29x) / (11) is the AWx>0-Anteil der zeitgleichen Netzeinspeisung aus dem Stromspeicher.
Formula (31x) = (30x) · (28x) is the förderfähige Netzeinspeisung von EE-Speichererzeugung for plant x in AWx>0 hours.
Formula (32x) = (26x) + (31x) is the insgesamt förderfähige Netzeinspeisung for plant x, monthly.
Formula (33x) = ∑J (32x) is the insgesamt förderfähige Netzeinspeisung for plant x, yearly.
Formulas (1)¼ and (2)¼ implement the gesetzlich gewillkürte vorrangige Zuordnung: on charging, grid supply is assigned first, and on discharging, storage generation is assigned first.
η_c and η_d are constant, non-calibrated inputs of each backtest and generate Z2V¼ and Z2E¼.
Formula (14) deviates from η_c · η_d whenever SOC crosses a month boundary.
Formula (14) is never fitted.
Formula (12) has no Ladepunkt source in A1 and can be positive only through SOC carried across the month boundary.
The source prints (29b) = ∑J (27b)¼, but by symmetry with (29a) and its own caption this is ∑M, and ∑M is what this repository uses.
Meters record energy per slot while engine variables are slot-average power, converted with Δt = 0.25 h in the meter-to-engine mapping and nowhere else.
P_net = Σ_k ( pv_avail[t,k] − q[t,k] ).
Z1NB¼ / Δt = MAX( 0, load + p_charge − P_net − p_discharge ).
Z1NE¼ / Δt = MAX( 0, P_net + p_discharge − load − p_charge ).
Z2V¼ / Δt = p_charge.
Z2E¼ / Δt = p_discharge.
Z1NB¼ · Z1NE¼ = 0, because one Zweirichtungszähler cannot import and export in one slot.
(Z1NB¼ − Z1NE¼) / Δt = load + p_charge − P_net − p_discharge, which is the POI bridge.
Off-take is not a control: load is fixed and no flexible loads are in scope.
Curtailment is a priced decision and never a deterministic rule, and its effect changes branch inside the same solve.
Raising q by one unit while exporting with Z1NE ≤ Z2E gives ∂(3) = 0, ∂(9) = 0, ∂(2)¼ = −1 and ∂(23)¼ = 0.
Raising q by one unit while exporting with Z1NE > Z2E gives ∂(3) = 0, ∂(9) = 0, ∂(2)¼ = 0 and ∂(23)¼ = −1.
Raising q by one unit while importing with Z1NB < Z2V gives ∂(3) = +1, ∂(9) = +1, ∂(2)¼ = 0 and ∂(23)¼ = 0.
Raising q by one unit while importing with Z1NB ≥ Z2V gives ∂(3) = +1, ∂(9) = 0, ∂(2)¼ = 0 and ∂(23)¼ = 0.
There are four curtailment regimes, each selected by which side of a MIN is active.
The same four-regime structure holds for aFRR down-activation, which is grid-driven charging.
No lever may carry a delineation coefficient of its own.

The delineation machinery is monthly while the decision is quarter-hourly: (16), (18), (30) and (32) are calendar-month sums and ratios, so a quarter-hour action is valued only through its effect on the month's aggregate.
H_plan truncation and the separable V_del must carry the monthly aggregation of the delineation machinery.
Formula (11), the storage energy that reached the grid, is what both routes compete for, and it splits at the PV-attributed share of storage generation.
(28) = MIN[ (11) ; (6) · pv_share ] is the green route.
(16) = MAX[ (11) − (6) · pv_share ; 0 ] is the grey route.
When (9) = 0, that is with no grid charging, (31) = (29): the ratio cancels and the green route is a per-slot linear sum.
When load = 0, the connection never clips discharge and (12) = 0, then (16) + (19) = (9) = (3) and therefore (21) = 0 identically.
When (12) > 0, relief falls by (12) / η_rt.
(12) = 0 is arithmetically impossible to violate once monthly charge throughput exceeds η_d · E_usable / (1 − η_rt), approximately 8 charge-equivalent cycles.
Discharging into load forfeits both routes: such a kWh never enters (11), so it earns neither (30) · premium nor levy_rate / η_month.
The forfeiture of both routes by discharging into load is priced by the state equations and not by a term.
Green and grey energy are identical everywhere behind the meter and differ only at injection to the grid.
Green energy becomes förderfähige Netzeinspeisung (32), in A5 per plant (32x), settled at that plant's AW and only in AW>0 quarter-hours via (24)¼.
Grey energy becomes saldierungsfähige Netzeinspeisung (16), which through (20) and (21) reduces the umlagebelasteter Netzbezug to zero in its own amount.
No Umlagen are levied on the saldierungsfähige Netzeinspeisung.
Formula (19)A1 extends the same relief to the privilegierungsfähige Stromspeicherverluste per § 21 EnFG, in the share (18).
